one_month_reasoning: There is no Synopsys print in Oct 2-31. FY26 Q4 results come in early December, and the defendants' response in the consolidated securities class action is due Nov 4 (10-Q), so both fall outside the window. Three things do fall inside it. (1) The FOMC on Oct 27-28. The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on Sep 16, unanimously, with August CPI at 3.4% y/y, and 16 of 18 participants expect at least one more hike in 2026. Another hike, or hawkish guidance, would hit long-duration names like SNPS, so I tilt slightly negative. (2) Cadence Q3 results around Oct 26 (date unconfirmed), a read-across on EDA demand in either direction. (3) The start of the ~$1B buyback. Short-horizon effects pull against each other. Drift after the guidance surprise, plus target raises (BofA $600, KeyBanc $605, Rosenblatt $620, BNP to $475 from $420), supports the price. Reversal after a ~31% two-week run, and the pattern of selling into strength (after the August beat the stock fell ~10% in a week), weigh on it. Short interest is ~5.7M shares, about 3% of float. My median is ~$488, a touch below spot for the FOMC risk, with monthly sigma ~12.5% (45%/3.5, trimmed slightly because no company event falls in the window), so the spread is roughly symmetric in log terms. I removed the CEO's Sep 15 sale as a signal: it was under a 10b5-1 plan.

fair_value.method: Blend of 75% P/E (FY28E non-GAAP EPS of $22.7 x 24x = $545) and 25% FCF yield net of SBC (FY28E FCF of $3.7B minus ~$1.05B SBC, at a 3.0% yield, less ~$4.9B net debt, over 189M shares = $441). Both are values as of Oct 2027.

methods.name: P/E
methods.inputs: FY28E non-GAAP EPS $22.7 (NTM at Oct-2027) x 24x

inputs_detail.derivation: $19.08 x 1.19. This is below the ~23% a year the framework implies after FY27, and below BofA's estimate, which it raised 16% after the event. I keep a haircut because management missed its Design IP outlook in 2025 (now a live class action), because non-GAAP excludes ~$970M of SBC and Ansys amortization, and because part of the EPS growth comes from buybacks. I nudged it up from 18% after the supervisor showed the framework implies ~23%.

Today's multiple is 25.7x the FY27 guide ($490.54/$19.08). Cadence trades at ~41x, and SNPS's own history runs ~40x to ~30x to ~25.7x. The Fed hiked to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16 and its median dot is 4.1% at end-2027 (no cuts), which argues against a re-rating and for a slight de-rating. ~$10B of gross debt and China/export-control exposure point the same way.

methods.name: FCF yield
methods.inputs: FY28E FCF $3.7B less SBC ~$1.05B = $2.65B; 3.0% yield gives EV $88.3B; less net debt ~$4.9B gives equity $83.4B; 189M shares

inputs_detail.derivation: $3.1B x ~1.2, below the mid-20s FCF CAGR target.
FY27 guided SBC grown ~8-10%, treated as a real cost.

$10.04B debt minus $3.61B cash = $6.4B at Jul-2026 (10-Q). Subtract ~$3.8B of FCF over Q4 FY26 and FY27, then add back ~$1.5B+ of buybacks ($1B near-term program, up to 50% of FCF), restructuring and other uses. Revised from $4.5B per the supervisor's check.
191.6M outstanding at Jul-2026, against an FY27 guide of 190-192M. The buyback partly offsets SBC dilution.

A quality EDA duopoly with high-teens growth targets. 3.0% is set above Cadence's implied ~2.5% for leverage and execution risk; the higher policy rate argues against going lower. I cut the weight to 25% (from 40%) because the leg partly double-counts SBC: peers' non-GAAP P/E multiples already embed SBC-heavy accounting.

bear.story: The Investor Day targets prove too high. Design IP disappoints again on AI customization economics (the 2025 pattern behind the Section 10(b) and Section 11 suits), AI chip-design spend digests, an open-source or AI-native design shock repeats (Kimi K3 knocked ~8-9% off SNPS and CDNS in a day in Jul-2026), or China EDA export curbs return (China ~10% of revenue). FY27 EPS lands near $17.5, and with the Fed still hiking the multiple compresses to ~19x.

base.story: FY27 broadly delivered (~$18.8-19.1 EPS), and the market looks to FY28 EPS of about $22.7 at ~23-24x, a slight de-rating with policy rates at ~4% and no cuts. The buyback offsets dilution. The class action gets through motion-to-dismiss briefing with no material charge. The AWS and OpenAI deals help but do not yet prove that the business model has changed.

bull.story: AI-agent monetization and application-optimized IP show up in the numbers. EDA reaches 13%+ and IP 17%+ growth, margins head toward 50%, FY28 EPS reaches $24.5, and the multiple re-rates to ~28.5x. That is capped below Cadence's multiple by the higher rate regime.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $360, the stock would have given up the whole Investor Day re-rating and fallen through the 52-week low ($362.55), about 19x the FY27 guide of $19.08. That would most likely mean the guide has lost credibility (a Design IP miss or an FY27 cut at the December print, reinstated China EDA licensing, or a credible AI/open-source share-loss story) rather than ordinary 45%-vol noise. I keep $360 rather than the supervisor's $365: the Kimi K3 day shows a single scare can move the stock ~8%, so a level right at the old low could be hit on noise.

reasoning: Round 2. The supervisor confirmed my core facts: the FY27 guide (~$11.15B revenue, $19.08 non-GAAP EPS, $3.1B FCF), net debt of ~$6.4B, China ~10% of revenue, and a live class action with a response due Nov 4. It added three things I take on board. (a) The Fed hiked 25bp to 3.75-4.00% on 2026-09-16, unanimously, with CPI at 3.4% and the median dot at 4.1% through end-2027; I verified this via Chase. (b) The CEO's Sep 15 sale was under a 10b5-1 plan, so I no longer treat it as a signal. (c) My Oct-2027 net debt should be ~$4.9B, not $4.5B. I also accept that a 40% weight on the SBC-burdened FCF leg partly double-counts SBC, and cut it to 25%. My skeptic-lane follow-ups: Kimi K3 is verified in Yahoo Finance (SNPS/CDNS -~9% on 2026-07-17; Bloomberg Intelligence saw no immediate revenue threat but a possible shift of value up the stack). The class actions include Securities Act Section 11 claims from ex-Ansys holders, which carry a lower bar than 10(b). Even so, typical settlements are small against a ~$93B market cap, so this is a headline and multiple risk, not a valuation hole. BNP Paribas Exane, a former Underperform, moved to Neutral at $420 on Sep 24 and to $475 after Investor Day, still below spot. Short interest has risen to ~5.7M shares (~3% of float). MarketBeat also lists HSBC and KeyCorp downgrades on 9/25 that contradict their Oct 1 raises (HSBC Buy $700, KeyBanc Overweight $605 per 24/7 Wall St). I treat those entries as aggregator errors and do not use them. Valuation: P/E $545 (FY28E $22.7 x 24x, with the multiple cut from 25x for the rate regime and the EPS raised from $22.5) and SBC-burdened FCF $441, weighted 75/25, give $519 (from $514). I stay below the supervisor's $540: a hiking Fed, a still-skeptical BNP and the history of de-rating argue against crediting the full framework. The scenarios are $330/$520/$700 at 25/50/25, a mean of ~$518. The ladder is a lognormal mix (85% median $498 with sigma 0.36, 15% median $420 with sigma 0.5 for the guidance-miss, China and AI-scare left tail). That gives P(>=$491) of 0.515, slightly below round 1's 0.525: the rate headwind and higher net debt outweigh dropping the CEO-sale signal. No option data and nothing under priors/ was consulted. Seeking Alpha, Benzinga and CNBC blocked fetching.
